newsitem.title: UK: London gold maintains upwards momentum early on.
newsitem.headline: London gold maintains upwards momentum early on.

text.p: Gold prices pushed higher early on Wednesday, buoyed by increasingly bullish market sentiment, dealers said.
"It's definitely looking firm. Every time it's moved up it has failed to fall back," a London-based dealer said.
"The market is cautiously bullish, and we may have seen the lows, at least for the next few weeks," he added.
Bullion fixed at $383.95 an ounce in the morning, versus $383.35 on Tuesday afternoon and up around $4.00 an ounce since the start of the week.
Prices started ticking higher on Monday when investment funds, most of them U.S-based, began covering their short positions, dealers said.
Despite market expectations of sharp declines, gold had stubbornly held above the key $380 support level over the past two weeks.
In early European trading gold edged steadily higher, building on gains posted in New York overnight. But it appeared to run into selling resistance just over $384 an ounce.

Dealers said gold may be unable to break out of a $380-$385 price range until after the end-of-month expiration of gold options, which give the right but not the obligation to buy or sell the metal at a given price.
"Actually, $385 isn't a technical level, it's just a round number. But it is significant because it's a key strike level for options," a dealer said.
In the event of gold breaking above $385 it would run into layers of stiff resistance between $386 and $388, which had provided buying support when prices were heading downhill.
Silver prices, indicated two cents firmer compared to Tuesday's London close at $4.98/$5.00 an ounce, were lagging behind gold's gains.
"A lot depends on silver. If it started breaking down it would cap gold's rise. But a break above the key $5.09-$5.11 area would probably take it up to $5.20," a dealer said.
Platinum was $1.70 firmer at $387.50/$388.50 an ounce, while palladium was $0.50 higher at $118.75/$119.75 after recovering from 3-1/2 year lows around $115 an ounce last week.
Dealers said the platinum group metals were absorbing strength from gold. But recent political uncertainty in Russia, a key producer of platinum and palladium, was also helping to boost prices.
